title: Transported: every convict ship to Australia, mapped
excerpt: Britain shipped about 162,000 convicts to Australia. I mapped all 745 voyages in Wikipedia's ship lists: the busiest port was Cork, the busiest year 1833, and the Second Fleet lost a quarter of its convicts at sea.
seo_description: A map of 745 convict voyages to Australia, 1788 to 1868: ports, passage times, deaths at sea, and penal transportation worldwide.
header_alt: Title card reading 'Transported' in black and red on pale paper, beside a world map with a thick braid of coloured lines running from the British Isles south through the Atlantic, round the Cape of Good Hope and across the Southern Ocean to Fremantle, Hobart, Sydney and Norfolk Island, and thinner lines from India and Mauritius. Below, a bar chart of ships arriving each year, rising to 35 in 1833. Text: every convict voyage to Australia in Wikipedia's lists, 745 ships, 1788 to 1868.
